newsitem.title: USA: Great Western says cost cuts to be shared.
newsitem.headline: Great Western says cost cuts to be shared.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp said Thursday the expense reductions anticipated in its proposed merger with Washington Mutual Savings Bank would be evenly split between the two firms.

Chief Executive John Maher, in a conference call with reporters, cited this as an advantage over a merger with H.F. Ahmanson and Co, which has said job losses in a merger would occur at Great Western.
"Ahmanson's bid was focused simply on cost savings," he said.
"There will be cost savings (in a Great Western-Washington Mutual deal) evenly distributed between the two respective companies, and less of an impact on Southern California than Ahmanson," he said.
In announcing their merger pact this morning, Great Western and Washington Mutual said they expected pre-tax expense reductions totalling $208 million in 1998 and $340 million in 1999.
Analysts have estimated job losses under the Ahmanson proposal would total about 2,500.
Maher also said he would retire as chief executive officer with the merger. He said he would be a member of the board of directors of the combined entity.
Maher said there was no comparison between Great Western's deal with Washington Mutual and the Ahmanson proposal.
"We have a definitive agreement with very clear-cut terms and we think it is in the best interest of shareholders.
"It's onward and upward (from here), and we have every intention of closing the deal," he said.
